## **Bugs and stability** {#theme-bugs_stability}

   **Bugs and stability.**
      2 recent review(s) mention bugs and stability.
      Review window: May 2, 2026 - Jun 23, 2026
      **Why it matters:** Users report reliability problems. This points to quality gaps competitors can exploit.

         **Review examples:**
            1. _Ivan nazvanov_, Jun 23, 2026, 1/5: "1 star. This is one of the most dangerous applications I have ever installed. I accidentally enabled All App Lock, fully confident that I could easily disable it within the app itself, or at least after uninstalling the app. But it turned out differently. After activating the lock, my iPhone literally turned into a brick for an hour. Almost nothing worked: applications were blocked, the camera would not open, the phone became practically useless. The worst thing is: deleting the application did NOT remove the lock. Even resetting the iPhone to factory settings did NOT help. I tried everything, including Screen Time settings, but to no avail. The only way to bring the phone back to life was to completely erase the device and restore from a backup. If I didn't have a backup, the consequences would be catastrophic. Developers, this is a critical issue. An app shouldn't be able to break the phone so deeply without an obvious emergency shutdown method. The user must have a clear emergency override: PIN, cancel timer, unlock button, or at least a warning in large text before activation. Now it looks not like a productivity tool, but like a potentially dangerous piece of software that can completely block your device. English (for developers): 1 star. This is one of the most dangerous apps I have ever installed. I accidentally activated the “block all apps” mode, fully expecting that I could easily disable it inside the app, or at least remove the restriction by deleting the app. That was not the case. After activation, my iPhone basically turned into a brick for an entire hour. Almost nothing worked. Apps were blocked, even the camera stopped working, and the phone became nearly unusable. The worst part: deleting the app did NOT remove the restriction. Even resetting iPhone settings to factory defaults did NOT help. I tried everything, including Screen Time settings, with no success. The only way to recover my phone was to completely erase the device and restore it from a backup. If I had no backup, this could have been catastrophic. Developers, this is a critical design flaw. No productivity app should be able to lock down a phone this aggressively without a clear emergency override. Users need a safe escape option: PIN override, cancel timer, unlock button, or at minimum a large warning before activation. Right now this feels less like a productivity tool and more like dangerous software capable of completely locking a device."
            2. _usobun_, May 2, 2026, 1/5: "Correct me if Im misunderstanding anything. This is coming from a developer of multiple years first of all let’s start off with how almost every single feature is paid. I know that the you developers need the payment to continue working on it well, but some features that are behind a paywall are GENUINELY necessities that shouldn’t cost a dollar. For example you can’t even intervention block more than a single app without getting the subscription, and if you tested the app well you would know that most people need to block more than 1 app. Surprise surprise if TikTok is blocked I’ll just switch to Insta. second I shouldn’t have to create a shortcuts automation every time I add an app to one sec. other focus apps allow you to block multiple apps in seconds. “linking” an app twice for each block/intervention is a bit redundant, it should just let me choose what apps i wanna block from a list. then there’s the fact there’s very little securing of your blocks unless you pay. it’s TOO easy to just delete the Shortcuts Automation to stop the app blocking forever, or just use the TikTok.com instead of the TikTok app (cause strict blocking is paid too…) It’s also REALLY annoying how a bug fix was turned into a Pro feature (Intentional App Switching). Normally if you got timed out from an app, you would close the app for 5 minutes, take a break, and come back after 5 minutes. Well with one sec you have to wait the full 5 minutes INSIDE the app to be able to use it again, or you’ll have to wait for the timeout to expire every, single time you reopen the app. Only way to fix this? get pro which is stupid The last straw was when the stupid intervention feature wasn’t working properly at all. I needed to use YouTube for an emergency but every time I went through the intervention YouTube was still blocked. Don’t make so many features paid if the basic ones aren’t even working properly. Developer, correct me if I misunderstood anything but in my opinion it’s not the most effective and a bit cash grabby. there are other focus apps like Opal with the same features for free"
